question: What is the primary focus of a Just Culture in healthcare settings?

options.A: Punishing every nurse who makes a clinical mistake
options.B: Encouraging incident reporting and learning from system failures
options.C: Ensuring total immunity for all healthcare professionals
options.D: Eliminating all forms of human error completely

explanation: A Just Culture focuses on creating a safe environment where errors can be reported so the organization can learn from system failures rather than immediately punishing individuals. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h1)

question: How does a Just Culture differ from a traditional blame culture?

options.A: It ignores all clinical mistakes made by staff
options.B: It shifts the focus from punishing individuals to examining systemic flaws
options.C: It holds no one accountable for reckless actions
options.D: It places 100 percent of the blame on hospital management

explanation: While a blame culture automatically disciplines the individual, Just Culture distinguishes between types of behaviors and looks closely at underlying systemic flaws. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h1)

question: What is a major consequence of operating within a traditional blame culture?

options.A: Nurses readily report all near misses and errors
options.B: Mistakes are hidden due to fear, leading to repeated patient harm
options.C: Systemic flaws are quickly and easily corrected
options.D: Patient safety improves drastically over time

explanation: In a blame culture, fear of punishment causes staff to hide errors and near misses, preventing the institution from identifying and fixing underlying systemic problems. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h2)

question: Why is a complete 'no-blame culture' considered unsafe in healthcare?

options.A: It promotes excessive documentation of nursing care
options.B: It increases the workload of nurse managers
options.C: It holds no one accountable, even for reckless and intentional safety violations
options.D: It prevents nurses from communicating with doctors

explanation: A pure no-blame culture fails because it grants total immunity, meaning reckless behaviors that endanger patients go unaddressed, which undermines overall safety. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary responsibility of hospital management under system accountability?

options.A: Punishing nurses immediately after any medication error occurs
options.B: Designing safe workflows, maintaining equipment, and providing adequate staffing
options.C: Monitoring every clinical action a nurse takes in real time
options.D: Covering up near misses to protect the hospital's reputation

explanation: System accountability requires management to build safe environments, provide functioning tools, and ensure proper staffing levels so workers can succeed. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h3)

question: When does individual accountability apply in the context of a Just Culture?

options.A: Whenever a patient experiences a negative health outcome
options.B: When a nurse makes an inadvertent slip while fatigued by poor scheduling
options.C: When a nurse makes a choice that deliberately or carelessly violates safety standards
options.D: Whenever hospital administration needs to cut nursing staff

explanation: Individual accountability holds nurses responsible for their personal behavioral choices, especially when they knowingly or carelessly disregard safety protocols. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h3)

question: How should nursing management typically respond to an isolated incident of human error?

options.B: Console the nurse and evaluate the system for flaws
options.C: Suspend the nurse's license for professional negligence
options.D: Publicly reprimand the nurse during shift handover

explanation: Human error is an unintentional slip, so the appropriate response is to console the affected staff member and investigate how the system can be improved to prevent recurrence. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following best describes reckless behavior in a clinical setting?

options.A: Accidentally misreading a physician's illegible prescription
options.B: Bypassing a safety protocol because the ward is critically understaffed
options.C: Coming to a hospital shift under the influence of alcohol
options.D: Forgetting to document a routine bed bath due to heavy patient load

explanation: Coming to work intoxicated represents a conscious and intentional disregard for safety, which defines reckless behavior and requires disciplinary action. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the Substitution Test in a Just Culture?

options.A: To find temporary replacement nurses during staff shortages
options.B: To determine if other competent nurses would make the same choice in the same situation
options.C: To test the clinical competency of newly graduated nursing students
options.D: To replace outdated hospital equipment with newer models

explanation: The Substitution Test evaluates an action by asking if other peers in the exact same conditions would likely have made the same mistake or choice. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h5)

question: If the Substitution Test reveals that multiple competent nurses would have acted similarly under the same working conditions, how is the event categorized?

options.A: As reckless misconduct requiring immediate termination
options.B: As gross negligence on the part of the individual nurse
options.C: As an understandable human error or systemic issue
options.D: As a criminal offense requiring police involvement

explanation: If peers would do the same thing under those conditions, it indicates a systemic or human error problem rather than individual recklessness. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h5)

question: What does psychological safety mean for nurses in a clinical unit?

options.A: The hospital building is structurally secure against intruders
options.B: Nurses can report errors and question orders without fear of humiliation or punishment
options.C: Patients are completely safe from contracting nosocomial infections
options.D: Staff members never experience physical fatigue during their shifts

explanation: Psychological safety creates an environment where staff feel safe to speak up, report mistakes, and question safety without fearing negative consequences. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h6)

question: How do strict hierarchical structures in healthcare often affect incident reporting?

options.A: They encourage junior nurses to report every minor mistake
options.B: They eliminate all forms of human error in clinical practice
options.C: They can make junior nurses hesitant to speak up or report errors made by senior staff
options.D: They automatically resolve systemic workflow issues

explanation: Steep hierarchies often intimidate junior nurses, causing them to fear retribution from seniors and leading to underreporting of critical errors and near misses. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is a major systemic challenge facing the Nigerian healthcare system that affects nursing practice?

options.A: An overabundance of fully staffed nursing wards
options.B: Severe staff shortages and resource constraints
options.C: The complete absence of medical equipment in all hospitals
options.D: Excessive salaries that reduce nurse motivation

explanation: Nigerian healthcare frequently deals with severe staff shortages, infrastructure issues, and resource constraints that create high-stress environments for nurses. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h7)

question: Why is it important to integrate Just Culture into Nigerian nursing school curricula?

options.A: To teach students how to discipline junior staff members effectively
options.B: To ensure graduates enter the workforce ready to advocate for safe systems and transparent reporting
options.C: To eliminate the need for clinical hospital placements during training
options.D: To focus entirely on punishing human errors in the classroom

explanation: Integrating Just Culture into nursing education prepares future nurses to promote transparent reporting and systemic safety once they enter clinical practice. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h7)
